title: Solar Physics and Space Weather
blurb: Solar image analysis, magnetic activity, and forecasting methods for understanding the Sun's eruptions and their effects.

person.name: C. Alex Young
person.expertise: Solar physics, signal and image processing, and space-weather communication
interests: solar flares and coronal mass ejections

papers.title: A Comparison of Flare Forecasting Methods. II. Benchmarks, Metrics, and Performance Results for Operational Solar Flare Forecasting Systems

notes.takeaway: Operational flare forecasts need shared benchmarks and metrics before systems can be compared.
notes.why: This paper makes evaluation part of the forecasting problem.

papers.title: Deep Learning Based Solar Flare Forecasting Model. I. Results for Line-of-sight Magnetograms

notes.takeaway: Deep models can learn flare precursors from line-of-sight magnetograms.
notes.why: It is a major bridge from magnetic images to prediction.

papers.title: Fine-grained Solar Flare Forecasting Based on the Hybrid Convolutional Neural Networks

notes.takeaway: Hybrid convolutional models target finer flare classes than a simple event/no-event label.
notes.why: Severity and lead-time detail matter operationally.

papers.title: Deep Learning Based Solar Flare Forecasting Model. II. Influence of Image Resolution

notes.takeaway: Image resolution changes what a deep flare forecast can learn.
notes.why: It exposes a measurement choice often hidden behind model scores.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Solar Flare Forecasting Model. III. Extracting Precursors from EUV Images

notes.takeaway: EUV images can carry precursor information complementary to magnetograms.
notes.why: Multi-wavelength imaging is central to Young's image-processing interests.

papers.title: Automatic Detection and Tracking of Coronal Mass Ejections. II. Multiscale Filtering of Coronagraph Images

notes.takeaway: Multiscale filtering helps detect and track diffuse CMEs in coronagraph images.
notes.why: It is a direct example of signal processing for space weather.

papers.title: Investigating the kinematics of coronal mass ejections with the automated CORIMP catalog

notes.takeaway: Automated catalogs turn CME tracks into kinematic measurements.
notes.why: Catalogs support statistics beyond individual case studies.

papers.title: Comparing Automatic CME Detections in Multiple LASCO and SECCHI Catalogs

notes.takeaway: Different automated catalogs do not necessarily identify the same CME population.
notes.why: Cross-catalog comparison is essential for trustworthy automation.

papers.title: A New Automatic Tool for CME Detection and Tracking with Machine-learning Techniques

notes.takeaway: Machine learning can automate CME detection and tracking in accumulated coronagraph data.
notes.why: It extends classical image processing toward scalable archives.

papers.title: Magnetic reconnection: MHD theory and modelling

notes.takeaway: MHD reconnection theory explains how magnetic topology changes and energy is released.
notes.why: It supplies the physical foundation behind flare signatures.

papers.title: Three-dimensional magnetic reconnection regimes: A review

notes.takeaway: Three-dimensional reconnection has multiple regimes rather than one simple geometry.
notes.why: It prevents image-based inference from collapsing complex topology into a cartoon.

papers.title: Observational studies of reconnection in the solar corona

notes.takeaway: Remote observations can test reconnection through coordinated morphology and dynamics.
notes.why: It connects theory to the observables Young works with.

sections.label: Magnetic energy and reconnection
sections.summary: Solar flares begin with magnetic energy stored in active regions. Reconnection theory and coronal observations explain how topology changes and energy reaches the plasma.
questions: Which observables distinguish competing reconnection regimes?

sections.label: From images to CME tracks
sections.summary: Solar images contain structure across scales and wavelengths. Filtering, catalogs, and machine learning turn those patterns into event and kinematic measurements.
questions: How can automated detections preserve uncertainty and physical context?

sections.label: Forecasting flares
sections.summary: Magnetograms and EUV images support forecasts, while benchmark design determines whether reported skill transfers to operations. Resolution, class imbalance, and lead time remain coupled choices.
questions: What should a forecast communicate to an operator besides a probability?

sections.label: Space weather decisions
sections.summary: The next step joins physical models, image pipelines, and alerts. A useful forecast must state its evidence, uncertainty, and likely consequence for Earth or spacecraft.
questions: How should uncertainty move from an image to an action?

opportunities: Compare detectors across LASCO, SECCHI, and newer imagers with shared event identities and uncertainty.
Combine magnetic topology, EUV structure, and calibrated learning rather than treating images as opaque pixels.
Evaluate forecasts by lead time, false-alarm cost, and the decision they support.

podcast.title: Reading the active Sun
podcast.description: From magnetic reconnection and solar images to CME catalogs and calibrated flare forecasts.
